subtopic: Money attitudes, family finances, gifting, borrowing between relatives
passage:
After dinner Rajni put a sheet of paper on the table beside the dal. "I want us to decide together how much I send and for how long." Her mother Sudha put down her spoon. Her younger brother's college fees would run for two more years, and her father's pension covered the rest of the household.
"I'll cover the fees each month until he finishes," said Rajni. "I'll also keep a fixed part of my salary in savings, so I don't panic if something happens. And in a year we look at it again."
Sudha's eyes filled. "We never wanted your life to shrink."
"It won't. Now the plan has an end date, so I don't have to feel guilty every month."
They wrote it out and put it on the fridge.

qa.q: How many more years will the brother's college fees run?
qa.a: The fees will run for two more years.

qa.q: What is Rajni feeling as she puts the paper on the table?
qa.a: She feels a mix of duty and worry about guilt, wanting a clear plan so she does not feel guilty every month.

qa.q: What made Rajni's plan a steady, guilt-free one?
qa.a: It set the amount and end date openly with the family, kept a fixed part of her salary for savings and included a review in a year.

qa.q: How does Sudha see Rajni's help?
qa.a: Sudha is moved, and says the family never wanted Rajni's life to shrink, so she welcomes the help but does not want Rajni to sacrifice her own future.

grounding: A young adult who earns decides openly with the family how much to give and for how long, keeping some savings.

passage:
"Two years of fees, Lavanya, ending when you finish your degree," said Aparna, tapping the notebook. "Then we look again."
"You don't have to, didi."
"I know. I want to. And I keep my own savings too, so I'm not resentful in March."
"If it's ever too much?"
"I'll tell you. And you tell me if you ever feel you owe me something you can't give."
Lavanya twisted the end of her dupatta. "I'll cook every Sunday."
"Deal. But study first."
"And when I'm working, I'll help Amma too."
"Only if you want to. Write the dates, will you?" Lavanya wrote 'review, December' at the top and drew a small star.

qa.q: How many years of fees did Aparna plan to cover?
qa.a: Aparna planned to cover two years of fees.

qa.q: What is Aparna feeling about supporting Lavanya, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Aparna feels willing and caring, shown by 'I want to', while keeping savings so resentment does not build.

qa.q: What made this arrangement a steady plan and not a heavy duty?
qa.a: They agreed a clear time period, a review in December, honest talking if it got too much, and savings for Aparna.

qa.q: How does Lavanya see the help her sister offers?
qa.a: Lavanya seems grateful and a little uneasy, saying she will cook every Sunday and later help Amma, as if she wants to give something back.

grounding: A young adult who earns decides openly with the family how much to give and for how long, keeping some savings.
